subject: System Design
title: Surge Pricing Explained
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Surge Pricing Explained.

hook.text: It's raining. Everyone wants a ride. Not enough drivers. Prices surge 3x. Suddenly, more drivers appear.

buildup.text: Surge pricing is dynamic: prices increase when demand exceeds supply to incentivize more drivers to get on the road.

discovery.text: Uber divides cities into hexagonal zones. Each zone calculates its own surge multiplier from local supply and demand.

twist.text: Surge also reduces demand: some riders choose to wait, take transit, or walk — balancing the market from both sides.

climax.text: Surge pricing is a real-time market mechanism that uses price to balance supply and demand dynamically.

punchline.text: Higher prices attract drivers and reduce riders — balance restored.

quiz.question: How does surge pricing balance supply and demand?
options: Higher prices attract more drivers while discouraging some riders
It forces all drivers to work
